failover._why: ask | auto | never, and JSON has no comments, so this key IS the comment. ask (the default) rings the repository lead with the approval command and is THE ONE UNAVOIDABLE HUMAN TURN in the whole design: nothing takes an agent's pane over until a person authorises it, which is exactly what happened the day this feature was written. auto APPLIES AND ANNOUNCES. That is not a loophole in the operator's no-silent-substitution rule and it should not be re-litigated: the rule forbids SILENT substitution, not substitution, and somebody who writes auto here has consented in advance, in writing, in config -- so the announcement to the lead is what keeps it non-silent, and it is sent every time. never refuses every INCIDENT-AUTHORISED takeover: `failover --incident <id>` is refused outright. It does NOT gate a bare `failover --run ... --agent ...` with no incident, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight -- consent is consulted only when an incident is supplied, because an operator typing the command at a keyboard IS the human turn this gate exists to demand, and a repository whose provider is genuinely dead must not have to edit config before it can recover. DETECTION IS UNAFFECTED BY THIS SETTING: the supervise tick records the incident under all three values, because an observation nobody acts on is still worth having.

idle_nudge._why: TM-408. The supervisor rings an idle standing agent through the safe bell (never over a draft or a tool prompt): a worker to ask its repository lead for its next assignment over the standing mailbox, a lead to take the next ready task from its own board. The census cannot tell an agent that finished from one that asked a human, so the guard is time: min_idle_ms (lead_min_idle_ms for a lead) of quiet counted from the end of its work. After a ring the agent is rung again only when the board's ready set changes or new mail arrives for it, and never sooner than backoff_ms, doubling per ring up to max_backoff_ms. retry_ms is how soon a refused ring is tried again. enabled false is the off switch.
